newsitem.title: USA: FOCUS-Intel falls on warnings over price cuts.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Intel falls on warnings over price cuts.

text.p: Intel Corp. stock fell Thursday as analysts raised alarms over the computer chip maker's upcoming price cuts that may mean the start of a price war amid weakening demand for personal computers.

The drop in the stock price of the world's biggest chip maker dragged down other computer stocks, which missed out on a blue-chip rally that lifted the Dow Jones industrial average 135.64 points to its fifth straight record at 7,711.47.
Intel fell as low as $142 early Thursday after Goldman Sachs & Co. and Cowen & Co. cut their 1997 earnings estimates for the company and Cowen downgraded the stock to neutral.
Intel edged off its lowest levels but still fell $3.84 to $143.66 on Nasdaq, where it was the most active issue, with over 18 million shares changing hands.

"I think the era of $500 processors in PCs is quickly coming to an end," said Drew Peck, a Cowen analyst. He cited competition from rivals such as Advanced Micro Devices Inc., which he said was forcing Intel to cut prices severely on products Intel has only just introduced.

"I think if the growth in the marketplace is going to be in the low end of the PC market, which is where it certainly is right now, you can't support more than $150 to $200 processor prices in a $1,000 box," he told Reuters.

Worries also persist over whether Intel's remarks over the past two weeks about weaker-than-expected demand, especially in Europe, signal a broader slowdown in PC sales just as the company has refreshed its product line.

Intel faces its strongest potential competition in years from rivals like AMD and Cyrix Corp. of Richardson, Texas, both of which are launching new processors. It also faces a massive patent infringement lawsuit brought by Digital Equipment Corp.

Cowen's Peck said Intel will slash prices for its mid-line 200 megahertz (MHz) Pentium MMX chip by 57 percent by November from its May price levels, and cut prices for the 166 MHz by 54 percent and the just-unveiled 233 MHz chip by 43 percent.
"That to me is a dramatic and fundamental change in the marketplace," he said. "Frankly, I think what they are doing is the right thing from the long-term perspective."
An Intel spokesman confirmed the company has begun distributing third-quarter price lists to customers. But he declined to discuss details until the changes take effect on July 28.
Intel's regular price cuts, which occur three times a year for consumer-end chips and every quarter for its higher-end processors, are closely watched as a barometer of the PC market's health.
Intel, which is one of the bellwether stocks in the technology sector, spooked Wall Street just two weeks ago by saying it expected second quarter results to fall below analysts' expectations.
